rules.statement: When a change alters how something is configured or behaves (for example, how a workflow pins an action), update every README, usage guide or other doc that describes the old behavior in the same change.
rules.why: Docs that contradict the code mislead maintainers into reverting the change. Here, docs that still described a tag pin could lead someone back to a tag pin, which brings back CodeQL's unpinned-tag alert.
rules.check: For each behavior or configuration the diff changes, search the README, USAGE and other docs for text that describes the old behavior. Report any statement the diff leaves stale.

rules.statement: Pin a third-party GitHub Action to a release's full commit SHA, with the release tag in a trailing comment, not to a tag alone.
rules.why: A tag pin triggers CodeQL's actions/unpinned-tag alert, because a tag can be moved.
rules.check: Look at `uses:` lines in workflow files. Report any that reference a tag or branch instead of a 40-character commit SHA followed by a tag comment.

rules.statement: Don't ask for a consumer-facing changelog entry to mention a test-only check or other internal test change that users of the package or template never see.
rules.why: The maintainer keeps test-only changes out of the changelog on purpose, because consumers aren't affected by them.
rules.check: Before reporting a changelog omission, check whether the omitted item only affects the repository's own tests or CI. If it does, don't report it.
